title: KPI heatmap and on-call escalation scripting for SLO incidents
creator: Nina Patel
description: Build a lightweight, actionable KPI heatmap that surfaces correlated signals for SLO incidents (burn rate, p95 latency, error-rate, KV cache hit rate, and request-rate) and wire it to an automated on-call escalation scripting layer. Goal: reduce noisy pages and accelerate mean time to acknowledge (MTA) by surfacing context and programmatically selecting the appropriate escalation path based on incident confidence and business impact.
acceptance_criteria: Heatmap dashboard shows per-route KPIs for at least 4 weeks of recent data and supports filtering by model, region, and customer tier
SLO burn-rate alert rules return a labeled alert with 'escalation_level' and 'heatmap_snapshot_url' when triggered
Alertmanager routing uses the 'escalation_level' label to choose between 'page', 'create-ticket', and 'notify-silent' with test coverage
A scripted escalation (bin/escalate-incident.sh) exists that can call PagerDuty with custom payloads and falls back to creating a Jira ticket when pager API returns 5xx
Canary for staging traffic for one week with synthetic load shows false-positive rate <= 8% and median time-to-context reduction >= 30%
Runbook documents (Confluence) linked from alert body and validated by on-call engineers
implementation_notes: Traces: reuse runtime trace hook to add 'route' and 'route.variant' tags at request start so SLO joins are reliable
Metrics pipeline: Prometheus -> Cortex recording rules for per-route burn-rate and p95; use 60s recording window to limit query cost
Logs: use Loki to capture last 5 error log lines per trace ID and attach a short URL to the heatmap snapshot
Anomaly detection: start with EWMA + seasonal-decomp thresholds in alert rule; prototype IsolationForest offline for noisy routes and evaluate cost
Alertmanager: add new label 'escalation_level' computed by Prometheus expression (burn_rate>10 -> critical, burn_rate>3 -> high, else low)
Escalation scripting: new binary in observability repo that accepts alert webhook, enriches with heatmap snapshot, and triggers PagerDuty/Jira per policy
Security: alert payloads must scrub PII; follow existing observability secret handling for PagerDuty API key via vault
Tracing correlation: reuse trace-correlation work from ENG-12047 to map traces -> SLO events in dashboard links
rollout_plan: Week 0: design review with SREs and a single product on-call (doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OBS/KPI+Heatmap+Design)
Week 1: implement recording rules and heatmap backend; instrumentation changes merged (PR #412)
Week 2: wire Alertmanager labels and implement escalate-incident script; staging canary deploy
Week 3: run synthetic load tests and collect false-positive metrics; iterate threshold tuning
Week 4: enable for limited production (non-critical routes) and invite on-call feedback; adjust paging policy
Post-rollout: retrospective and incident analysis; consider ML-based anomaly detector if noise remains high
comments: 2025-02-18 Nina Patel: Kickoff — scoped to heatmap UI + alert enrichment + escalation scripting. Decided to use Prometheus/Cortex for recording rules to keep compute near metrics store.

2025-02-20 Marco Li: Infra note — will add 'route.variant' tag at runtime start. Impact: small extra label cardinality but enables accurate joins for per-route SLOs. Measured increase ~2% cardinality in staging over 24h.

2025-02-24 Priya Shah (SRE): Proposed escalation policy matrix in design doc. Trade-off: strict paging reduces MTA but increases noise; agreed to start conservative (page only on critical burn-rate + p95 degradation).
2025-02-26 Marco Li: WIP PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/412 — adds recording rules, heatmap API, and example alert templates. Requesting review from @priya and @sam.

2025-02-28 Sam Ortiz (on-call): Tested escalation script locally. Script supports a '--dry-run' mode that returns the payload we would send to PagerDuty. Found formatting issues with heatmap snapshot URL; fixed in PR.

2025-03-01 QA: Canary run started in staging with 10 synthetic clients replaying failing traces. Early results: burn-rate alerts triggered as expected; one route had too many false positives due to bursty background jobs — adjusted EWMA alpha and increased min-sample window.

2025-03-03 Marco Li: Updated Alertmanager routing rules to include 'team_override' label so platform SREs can temporarily silence pages for noisy routes. Added playbook link to alert body: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OBS/Oncall+Escalation+Playbook

2025-03-04 Priya Shah: Runbook validated. Next: schedule 1-hour on-call table-top to walk through sample incidents and confirm timing and payloads. Also create follow-up ticket to prototype IsolationForest for top-10 noisy routes (ENG-13322).
open_questions: Do we want model-level SLOs included in the initial rollout, or only route-level? (PM preference: route-level first)
Should we invest in ML-based anomaly detection now or defer to an offline prototype after rollout?
What is the maximum acceptable paging noise rate for P1 incidents? (current target <= 8%)
next_steps: Finish code review on PR #412 and merge
Complete staging canary and collect false-positive/true-positive metrics for one week
Schedule on-call tabletop and gather feedback
Create follow-up ticket for IsolationForest prototype (ENG-13322) and for production rollout checklist
